metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth are tracked as an uptime and redundancy metric because distributed AI training wastes GPU-hours on a lossy fabric before any outage appears.

The metric is a continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit. It sits in the uptime and redundancy category alongside UPS battery health and generator runtime, and SLA uptime compliance. That grouping treats network quality as a resilience condition, not a separate performance concern.

For AI workloads, the cost of network degradation is measured in compute before it is measured in downtime. A lossy fabric consumes expensive accelerator time during distributed training, so this metric matters for the efficiency of GPU capacity, not only for keeping services online. The definition does not specify thresholds, measurement intervals, or which side of the fabric, internal or external, is the binding constraint.
